report.changes_to_report: The answers do not change my verdicts. They do make three points sharper. (1) Who chooses: the owner accepted 'the proposals behind these decisions' as a whole on 2026-10-31, and nothing records that the owner saw A04 r3's narrowing of the 'returns it unchanged' rows. The part of A04 r3 that the owner did accept says an erased Customer or an anonymised project 'states none'. So the accepted text answers only the stating-none case, which all alternatives agree on. The resubmitted erasure that states the erased-from revision (W01) is still undecided by any owner text. The owner still chooses. (2) keeps_accepted stays 'unsure'. The accepted histories are kept. Whether the S0 erase row is kept depends on reading it as 'stating none', and nothing records that the owner endorsed that reading. One neighbour claim in my report goes: I can no longer say the row becomes unreachable from the UI, because the owner interface is not decided before State 5. I withdraw that claim and do not replace it with a guess. W01 stays admissible anyway, because A04's Consequence (accepted) says the UI sends the revision of the card it rendered, which is the erased-from revision. (3) Counterexamples: counterexample 1 (lost answer, resubmitted erasure refused as stale after the erasure took effect) and counterexample 2 (stale answered with no revision to compare against) stand unchanged. Counterexample 3 (W13) is confirmed as ambiguous under the edit: A05 r4's 'come first' has no reading beyond its text, so R0-71's refusal may precede stage 5. A13 r6's binding for a record without a revision is undecided, so W11 and W13 may also stop at stage 1. Neither ambiguity arises under alternative B, which answers W13 by R0-71 under any reading of A05 r4.
report.why: A (stale), B (stage 5 skipped, so unchanged or erased) and C (invalid input) all keep every accepted history and every accepted passage read literally. They differ only in the answer the owner gets for the normal resubmission of a State 0 action whose recorded intent is 'a repeated erasure is a no-op'. That row predates R0-35. R0-35's wording ('a change against an older revision') does not reach a record with no revision. The owner's acceptance of A04 r3 is recorded only in aggregate, with no sign the narrowing was shown, and the accepted sentence itself exempts records without a revision ('states none'). RT.state2 lets State 2 choose which actions state a revision. It does not let State 2 turn a State 0 'returns it unchanged' into a refusal. So the choice belongs to the owner.
report.next_step: Both, in this order. First, put one question to the owner: 'When the form that erased a customer's contact data is submitted again (same card, its old revision), should Registry answer the customer unchanged, as a no-op (B), or refuse it as stale, with nothing changed (A)? Either way nothing is erased twice and no audit entry is written.' Offer C only as a variant of A if the owner prefers a distinct 'no revision expected' refusal. Second, apply the matching patch below once the answer is recorded with its date. Do not apply option_A.patch as it stands. Until the owner answers, W01, W02, W05, W06, W11 and W13 stay open.
